title: How Well Do You Know the Ten Commandments?
subtitle: Ten rules, one mountain, and a whole lot of history.
about: Ten short instructions, given on a mountain, still shape how billions of people think about right and wrong. They were never meant as a checklist for earning God's favor, but as a picture of a life shaped by love for Him and for other people.

verses.text: I am Jehovah thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

questions.text: On which mountain did God give Moses the Ten Commandments?

options.explanation: Exodus 19 and 20 place the giving of the Law at Mount Sinai, where God came down in fire and smoke.
Mount Carmel is where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal, long after Moses.
Mount Ararat is where Noah's ark came to rest, not where the Law was given.
The Mount of Olives belongs to the Gospels and the life of Jesus.

questions.text: What were the Ten Commandments written on?

options.explanation: They were not written on a scroll. They were carved into stone.
Exodus 31:18 says God gave Moses two tables of stone, written with the finger of God.
There was no bronze plate. The commandments were on stone tablets.
The tabernacle came later, and the commandments were carried inside it on stone tablets.
That command comes later in the list, not first.

options.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me
options.explanation: Exodus 20:3 says, "Thou shalt have no other gods before me" (ASV).

options.text: Honour thy father and thy mother
options.explanation: Honoring parents is a commandment, but it is not the first one.
The sabbath command is important, but it is not the first.

questions.text: Which commandment forbids making and bowing down to idols or carved images?

options.explanation: Exodus 20:4-5 forbids making a graven image and bowing down to it, which is the second commandment.
The fifth commandment is about honoring father and mother, not idols.
The eighth commandment is about not stealing.
The tenth commandment is about coveting, not making idols.

questions.text: The commandment about the sabbath day tells the people to do what?

options.text: Keep it holy and rest from work
options.explanation: Exodus 20:8-10 says to remember the sabbath, keep it holy, and do no work on it.
Daily offerings were part of other laws. The sabbath command was about rest.
The command was to rest and keep the day holy, not to travel anywhere.
The sabbath was about rest, not fasting.

questions.text: Which commandment comes with a promise of long life?

options.explanation: This command is vital, but it does not carry the promise of long days in the land.

options.text: Honour thy father and thy mother
options.explanation: Exodus 20:12 says to honor your father and mother, that your days may be long in the land.
This command stands on its own without the promise of long life.
The promise of long life is tied to honoring parents, not to coveting.

questions.text: Which of these is one of the Ten Commandments?

options.text: Thou shalt not lie with thy neighbor's ox
options.explanation: That is not a commandment. The list says do not covet your neighbor's possessions, including his ox.

options.text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour
options.explanation: Exodus 20:16 says, "Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor" (ASV).

options.text: Thou shalt give a tenth of all thou hast
options.explanation: Tithing appears elsewhere in the Law, but it is not one of the ten.

options.text: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself
options.explanation: That command is from Leviticus 19:18 and was quoted by Jesus, but it is not in the list of ten.

questions.text: Which command warns against wrongly using the name of God?

options.text: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain
options.explanation: Exodus 20:7 says not to take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
Adultery is its own commandment and is not about God's name.
Stealing is a separate commandment with nothing to do with God's name.
The sabbath command is about resting, not about the use of God's name.

questions.text: The tenth commandment is about which sin of the heart?

options.explanation: Pride is a sin Scripture warns about, but the tenth commandment names a different one.

options.text: Coveting what belongs to your neighbor
options.explanation: Exodus 20:17 says not to covet your neighbor's house, wife, servants, or anything that is his.
Anger is addressed elsewhere, but the tenth commandment is about coveting.
Laziness is not the subject. The tenth commandment forbids coveting.

questions.text: What did Moses do with the first set of tablets when he came down and saw the golden calf?

options.text: He hid them in the ark
options.explanation: He did not hide them. In his anger he broke them.
Exodus 32:19 says Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them at the foot of the mount.

options.text: He read them aloud to the people
options.explanation: He did not read them first. Seeing the calf, he threw the tablets down and broke them.
He did not hand them to Aaron. He shattered them in anger over the calf.

questions.text: After the first tablets were broken, where did the second set end up being kept?

options.text: In the ark of the covenant
options.explanation: Deuteronomy 10:5 says Moses put the tables in the ark he had made, and there they remained.
The altar of incense had its own purpose. The tablets went into the ark.
They were not stored in a tent. They were placed in the ark of the covenant.
Nothing was buried at Sinai. The tablets were carried in the ark.

scoring.perfectMessage: A perfect score. You know all ten by heart.

gradeBands.label: Seeker
gradeBands.message: Worth a fresh look. You can read the whole list in Exodus 20.

gradeBands.label: Student
gradeBands.message: You know the big ideas. A little more reading and the order will stick.

gradeBands.label: Scholar
gradeBands.message: You know the commandments well. Solid work.

gradeBands.label: Sage
gradeBands.message: Few know the Law this well. Wonderfully done.
